title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-04-06
content:
Quick log - 2026-04-06

Morning:
- Coffee, triage queue. Priorities: KV cache leak, unstable kernel fallback on A100-80GB, perf regression on 2-token warmup path.
- Standup notes: sync w/ Ravi at 10:30 on KV leak repro. Maya to run microbench for kernel selection thresholds.

Today goals (high level):
1) Narrow down root cause of KV cache memory growth (regression introduced ~PR 1260) - repro, minimal test, hotfix if trivial.
2) Add telemetry for kernel selection decision path (want to know fraction of requests hitting fallback kernels).
3) Perf TODOs: tune continuous batching flush thresholds; validate impact on p95 for <64 tokens.

Triage notes:
- JIRA-ENG-3421: KV cache not releasing under high multiplexing. Repro steps in ticket. Observed: host RSs show steady rss increase ~20MB/min after 2h load. Possibly cache eviction not honored when batch merging occurs.
  - Hypothesis: race between batch merge and cache eviction pass; eviction iterates over shards but merged requests keep references.
  - Next: create minimal harness to run concurrent merge + eviction loop (Ravi). If repro, add temp lock around eviction to confirm.
  - Linked PRs: PR 1260 (batch merge rewrite) may have touched shard pointer lifecycle.

- JIRA-ENG-3478: A100-80GB kernel fallback - sometimes falls back to generic kernel causing 2x latency for long sequences. Failure pattern: memory allocator returns different device pointer, kernel selection checks alignment and rejects optimized kernel.
  - Action: add extra logging for allocator ptr alignment and kernel selection rationale (Maya). Add unit test simulating allocator fragmentation.

Perf TODOs / experiments:
- Microbench plan (Maya): run kernel selection microbench across models {redwood-7b, redwood-13b, llama2-13b} on A100 vs H100; measure selection distribution and latency. Timeline: 1 day.
- Batching: current flush threshold: 16ms or 32 tokens. Hypothesis: lower flush time for small seqs helps p95 at cost of throughput. Experiment: try 8ms flush + adaptive increase under high qps. Metrics to capture: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99.
- KV prefix caching: evaluate cache hit rate on canary traffic. If hit-rate < 0.2 then consider disabling prefix cache for low-context flows.

Kernel notes / ideas:
- Consider adding a soft-degarde path: if optimized kernel fails validation more than N times in M seconds, mark it "degraded" and prefer fallback for a bit, avoid repeated failure logs.
- We should persist kernel health state per-host in memory (ephemeral) with exponential backoff for re-enable. Keep counters in state store keyed by kernel-id.

Commands / quick snippets:
- repro harness (local): ./bazel-bin/serving/tests/kv_leak_harness --workers=64 --duration=7200 --merge-interval-ms=5
- run kernel microbench: scripts/bench-kernel.sh --model redwood-7b --device a100 --iters 5000 --seq-len 1024
- gather logs from canary: gcloud logging read "resource.type=container AND labels.k8s-pod/app=serving-canary" --limit 1000 > canary-logs-2026-04-06.log

Notes from 10:30 sync with Ravi:
- Repro is flaky locally; repros reliably on k8s canary. Plan: deploy instrumented container with extra memstats and eviction logging. Use a rolling canary to avoid customer impact.
- Temporary mitigation: reduce batch-merge concurrency to 8 on canary nodes (config flag batch_merge_concurrency). Might reduce throughput but may stop leak while we debug.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is PR 1260 revert needed if we can hotfix eviction ordering? Prefer minimal change.
- How to surface kernel health to Console dashboard? Need an API: /metrics/kernel_health with simple counters. Ask Console team for a slot in next sprint.

Action items (owners):
- RAVI: build minimal repro harness + deploy instrumented canary (ETA EOD).
- MAYA: run kernel microbench + add allocator alignment logging (ETA tomorrow morning).
- SAM: add temporary config to reduce batch_merge_concurrency on canary and a small hotfix to eviction ordering if repro validated (ETA 24-48h).
- Follow-up sync tomorrow 09:00 to review logs and decide on hotfix vs revert.

Misc scratch (brain dump):
- Might be worthwhile to snapshot allocator ptr distribution over time to see fragmentation pattern.
- If eviction is blocked by in-flight merged-requests, consider marking those requests as weak-refs in shard map so they don't pin memory indefinitely. Needs careful GC semantics.

End of scratchpad.
